## Technical Skills & Proficiencies
- **Offensive Security & Red Teaming:** Network scanning (Nmap), vulnerability assessment (Nuclei, OpenVAS), exploitation (Metasploit Framework, manual PoC exploits), web application security (Burp Suite Professional, SQLMap, CSRFShark, OWASP ZAP), Linux privilege escalation, reverse engineering & decompilation (JADX-GUI, MobSF).
- **Web Application Penetration Testing:** OS command injection, SQL injection, cross-site scripting (Reflected, Stored, DOM), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), authentication bypasses, broken object level authorization (BOLA), session management flaws, password reset poisoning via host headers.
- **AI & LLM Security:** Prompt injection auditing, indirect prompt injection vectors via untrusted content, excessive agency exploitation in LLM tool calling, API authentication leakage, model alignment evaluation.
- **Development & DevOps:** Vanilla HTML5/CSS3/Modern JavaScript (ES6+), Python, Node.js, Git, Cloudflare DNS & Edge Network configuration, GitHub Pages hosting, Docker.

## BugXploit 14-Day Ethical Hacking Workshop Archives
- **Location:** BugXploit Training Center, Koteshwor, Kathmandu, Nepal
- **Instructor Profiles:**
  - Birendra Sah (Cybersecurity Specialist & Trainer): https://www.linkedin.com/in/birendrasah4u2/
  - Bishal Shrestha (Security Researcher & Red Teamer): https://www.linkedin.com/in/bishal0x01/
- **Documentation Author:** Chandan Kumar Thakur (TheWH2)

### Session Summaries
1. **Session 1:** Lab setup using Oracle VM VirtualBox on Windows/Linux host, deploying Kali Linux 2026 and Metasploitable 2 in an isolated Host-Only network adapter, ICMP ping testing, terminal reconnaissance, and understanding Bugcrowd vulnerability disclosure target programs.
2. **Session 2:** Nmap scanning methods (`nmap -sV -sC -p-`), identifying vulnerable VSFTPD 2.3.4 daemons, exploiting CVE-2011-2523 to trigger a backdoor root listener on TCP port 6200, Telnet plain-text sniffing, and SSH brute-forcing using Metasploit.
3. **Session 3:** OSINT reconnaissance, target scope discovery, Google Dorking operators (`site:`, `filetype:`, `intitle:`), DNS records using DNSDumpster, SSL certificate logs using crt.sh, WHOIS lookups, email spoofing validation via SPF/DKIM records, Shodan queries, and Wayback Machine snapshot extraction.
4. **Session 4:** Remote OS command injection against DVWA on low and medium security tiers, Netcat interactive reverse shell handlers (`nc -lvnp 4444`), Burp Suite proxy intercept, manipulating GET/POST parameters, token bypasses, and CSRFShark proof-of-concept exploits.
5. **Session 5:** Burp Suite Intruder Sniper mode automated password attacks, SQLMap automated database extraction (`--dbs`, `--tables`, `--dump`), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) fundamentals (Reflected, Stored), client-side input validation bypasses, and session cookie stealing using Webhook.site.
6. **Session 6:** Automated vulnerability assessment with ProjectDiscovery Nuclei against target hosts, triage of 69 security findings, PHP-CGI query execution (CVE-2012-1823), Samba (CVE-2026-4480), GitHub secret reconnaissance dorks, and validating leaked API tokens using streaak/keyhacks.
7. **Session 7:** Android mobile penetration testing, Java Development Kit (JDK 26), JADX-GUI decompilation, MobSF static analysis of DivaApplication.apk, finding Janus vulnerability (CVE-2017-13156), identifying exported Android components, and dumping hardcoded application secrets.
8. **Session 8:** PortSwigger Web Security Academy authentication vulnerabilities, subtle response-length username enumeration, IP rate-limit bypass with JSON array credentials, broken 2FA logic, password reset token parameter stripping, and password reset poisoning via HTTP Host header injection (`X-Forwarded-Host`).
9. **Session 9:** Web LLM Attacks, exploring Large Language Model integration risks, Prompt Injection techniques, exploiting excessive agency to manipulate database queries via chatbot tool executions, and Indirect Prompt Injection through tainted data in customer reviews.

10. **Session 10:** Live bug bounty hunting reconnaissance on HackerOne targeting Sony (VDP scope), mapping corporate hierarchies and acquisitions using Crunchbase, passive DNS enumeration with DNSDumpster, analyzing application request flows, probing search inputs for HTML injection and contextual XSS encoding, executing advanced Google dorking queries, inspecting JSON Web Token (JWT) architecture on JWT.io, testing URL parameter open redirect bypasses against whitelist filters, and provisioning isolated test accounts using Temp-Mail.
